instructions: Heat the oven to 390°F. Rub the insides of four 10 oz ramekins with a little butter and set them on a baking sheet.
Thinly slice the 8 oz mushrooms and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Strip and chop 2 tsp thyme leaves.
Melt the 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium high. Add the mushrooms in an even layer and cook for about 3 minutes, stirring once or twice, until the edges turn golden.
Add the garlic, thyme, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/8 tsp pepper and cook for 1 minute, until the garlic smells fragrant.
Add the whole bag of spinach and stir for about 30 seconds, only until it wilts. Take the pan off the heat.
Divide the mushrooms and spinach between the ramekins and press a small dip into the middle of each. Crack 1 egg into each dip.
Spoon 1 tbsp cream over each egg, then grate the parmesan and scatter 1 tbsp over each one.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still jiggle when you nudge the sheet. Check at 12 minutes. Take them out a touch early. They keep cooking in the hot ramekins.
While they bake, slice the baguette and toast it. Finely chop 2 tsp chives.
Dust the eggs with the 1/8 tsp smoked paprika and scatter the chives on top. Serve hot with the toast.
method_notes: All three bake eggs in buttered ramekins with cream over the top until the whites set and the yolks are still runny. RecipeTin Eats puts each egg on a bed of garlicky mushrooms and spinach, tops it with parmesan and bakes at 390°F without a water bath for 12 to 15 minutes. Food Faith Fitness and The Daily Meal keep it to eggs, cream and seasoning and bake in a water bath at 350°F, The Daily Meal under foil, for 12 to 20 minutes. All serve them with toast or bread for dipping.
